name: G V Electricals
sector: Electrical utility operations, maintenance and infrastructure services
summary:
G V Electricals is a labour-intensive power-distribution services contractor, not an electrical-product manufacturer. Its most credible attraction is recurring operations and maintenance work: this generated 76.90% of FY26 sales, and 88.29% of sales came from repeat customers. Revenue reached ₹156.41 cr and PAT ₹10.47 cr, while the August IPO supplied real fresh equity. The decisive weakness is the gap between those earnings and realizable cash: FY26 CFO was −₹3.31 cr, receivables rose to ₹51.16 cr and bank-reported collateral values differ materially from the books. These are operational, financial-reliability and funding questions, not matters a low headline P/E resolves.

At the 19 October 2026 secondary completed close of ₹114.30, current equity value is ₹128.92 cr and post-issue FY26 P/E 12.32×. An explicitly conditional five-year base model returns 10.40%, below the 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle; the model's base hurdle price near ₹93 is not an actionable buy level while G2 and G3 are unresolved. BQS, Growth Quality Score (GQS) and IAS remain NS, not weakly precise point scores. This is a research-watchlist contract-services growth candidate, not an established compounder or a governance-fraud verdict. A bank-accepted asset reconciliation, a verified post-IPO cash/utilization bridge, clean collections and attributable incremental contract economics would materially change the assessment.
priority: Research watchlist — reliability and funding evidence required
thesis_type: Working-capital-funded contract-services growth; not an established compounder
identity_note: BSE544859, listing12 August2026; primary master confirms ISIN/shares/1,000-share lot. NSE master is interoperable coverage, not NSE listing.

quote.kind: Completed daily close, secondary; primary bhavcopy unavailable

score_note: GQS means Growth Quality. CAP/R/L missing; Q inherits missing BQS. No imputation or renormalization. GQS completion capped5 for persistent CASH2.

gates.reason: Repeated compliance/control problems and connected-history scrutiny, but no established severe diversion or manipulation. GOV 4; no automatic governance Avoid override.

Material bank-return/books differences lack a quantitative bank-accepted reconciliation. The annual-report/prospectus auditor-resignation inconsistency is an additional disclosure control concern. Unmodified opinion is retained as contrary evidence, not ignored.

Completed net IPO fresh funding is real, but remaining cash, actual debt repayment, eligible drawing power and continued facilities are not verified. Positive hypothetical cash paths do not resolve financing; neither do stress failures prove actual default.
Exact identity and 1,000-share eligible SM lot verified; new listing has insufficient 60-session history and primary traded-value series was inaccessible. No evidence of suspension; L remains NS.

factor_audit.name: Governance and minority protection
supporting_facts: Recurring GST/PF/ESIC delays across multiple years and ₹0.7346 cr FY26 charges weaken compliance confidence.
FY24 connected advances of ₹4.9273 cr were material to ₹17.0507 cr equity; bank reporting and auditor-resignation disclosures need reconciliation.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Connected advances were repaid by FY26; audit reports no fraud noticed or lender default, and disqualified independent director was replaced publicly.
factor_audit.rationale: 4 reflects substantiated control weaknesses, not an unsupported allegation of diversion. Evidence does not meet the severe GOV≤3 automatic Avoid threshold.

factor_audit.name: Defensibility and customer economics
supporting_facts: O&M is 76.90% of sales and repeat business 88.29%, supporting operational familiarity.
Four decades of experience and multi-state technical deployment support tender qualification.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Top customer 33.33%, top ten 94.76%; price competition follows technical qualification, without patented technology or guaranteed volumes.
factor_audit.rationale: 4: execution relationships create some friction, but neither pricing power nor superior customer-level returns is independently established.

factor_audit.name: Revenue growth and scale
supporting_facts: FY23–FY26 revenue CAGR 14.49% uses three actual year intervals.
Annual additions expand from ₹7.57 cr to ₹19.44 cr to ₹25.18 cr; FY26 growth 19.18%.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Metering falls 23.08% in FY26 and no two comparable recent halves/four quarters establish an acceleration adjustment.
factor_audit.rationale: 6 follows the 10–15% three-year CAGR anchor. Four-year un-restated revenue triangulation and FY26 jump do not override the preferred consistent series.

factor_audit.name: Duration and reinvestment runway
supporting_facts: O&M renewal work is recurring in nature, and ₹553.70 cr headline frameworks span multiple projects.
Power distribution upkeep, metering and network work provide continuing demand rather than one factory order.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Rate contracts do not guarantee volumes, repeat share declined, and Odisha contributes 69.05% of sales.
factor_audit.rationale: 6 recognizes a medium-duration service runway while discounting concentration and conditional call-offs. Data-centre plans are optionality, not contracted growth.

factor_audit.name: Incremental capital economics
supporting_facts: The FY23–FY26 operating and financing IC bridges reconcile at ₹15.0487 cr and ₹54.0880 cr.
The 33%-tax ΔNOPAT/ΔIC proxy is 19.98%; disclosed investment and ONWC changes reconcile to ΔIC.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: 84% of EBIT improvement is mechanically attributable to margin change on the end-period revenue base, not clearly to new contracts.
factor_audit.rationale: NS rather than a neutral score: cash realization, bank-collateral values and mature contract profitability are insufficient to validate incremental reinvestment returns.
factor_audit.missing_evidence: Project/cohort capital, renewal-level margin, collection realization and a bank-accepted current-asset reconciliation.

factor_audit.name: Earnings realization
supporting_facts: Three-year CFO/PAT is −10.27%; four-year ratio −4.88%, not an average of annual ratios.
FY26 ₹20.27 cr receivable absorption dominates the operating cash shortfall; three-year total-capex FCF is −₹8.948 cr.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Receivables older than six months fell materially, and IPO funding can bridge the collection cycle if properly used.
factor_audit.rationale: 2: persistent poor realization is evidenced. CFO is weak because of operating balances, not because capex directly depresses CFO. CASH≤3 imposes a GQS ceiling of 5 but does not fill missing CAP.

factor_audit.name: Balance-sheet resilience
supporting_facts: May cash credit is 99.61% utilized and FY26 debt more than doubles to ₹16.47 cr.
₹6.76 cr gratuity and substantial tax/payroll claims reduce freely distributable resources; all FD is prudentially excluded from cash.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: The completed IPO brought ₹33.49 cr net fresh equity, and FY26 operating interest coverage is 11.73×.
factor_audit.rationale: 4 balances demonstrated pre-IPO working-capital strain against a real equity raise. It does not grant a funding pass without actual utilization, renewal and liquidity evidence.

factor_audit.name: Execution and delivery record
supporting_facts: Revenue increased each observed year with broad field-service deployment.
Disclosed ongoing contracts and repeat customers support ability to deliver routine services.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: No clean backlog execution bridge or completion/renewal certificates for recently expiring contracts were obtained; compliance delays remain recurrent.
factor_audit.rationale: 5 is mixed execution evidence, not an award for announced order size. Contract expiry alone is not treated as a missed promise.

factor_audit.name: Quality of earnings growth
supporting_facts: Operating EBITDA increases from ₹8.04 cr to ₹17.05 cr, well beyond the 19.18% revenue increase.
Other income is only ₹0.2481 cr, so FY26 profit is not chiefly an investment-income story.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Margin sustainability is unproven, earlier profits were materially restated and deferred-tax credits reduce book tax. Current-share EPS is only ₹9.28 versus reported pre-IPO ₹12.64.
factor_audit.rationale: 5: genuine reported operating expansion, but fragile attribution and weak cash realization preclude a high-quality earnings-growth score.

factor_audit.name: Five-year return spread
supporting_facts: The full five-year base cash path yields 10.40%, below the 15% hurdle, conditional on the opening bridge.
A combined collection and opening-cash stress fails the minimum cash test in year 1; all ordinary returns remain null until financing is verified, including cash-positive hypothetical paths.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Bull scenario can exceed the hurdle and fresh IPO proceeds are real, not hypothetical fundraising.
factor_audit.rationale: NS: useful scenario arithmetic is not a fundable expected-return case. Material post-IPO cash, collateral and facility continuation remain unverified.
factor_audit.missing_evidence: Actual post-IPO balance sheet/cash-flow and utilization statement; sanctioned versus drawn and eligible facilities.

factor_audit.name: Capital-loss protection
supporting_facts: Hypothetical bear terminal value is about ₹62.30/share, a 45.50% capital decline despite no assumed insolvency.
Customer concentration, receivable delays and creditor normalization can combine into an early funding shortfall.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Completed equity funding and substantial current receivables could preserve operating continuity if collections are confirmed.
factor_audit.rationale: 3: limited downside protection. A low earnings multiple does not protect against working-capital impairment and dilution.

factor_audit.name: Expectations embedded in price
supporting_facts: Current-share trailing P/E is 12.32×, but on the single high-margin FY26 result.
At base economics the 15% hurdle requires roughly 17.57% revenue CAGR versus the lower base path; margin/exit assumptions have large impact.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: A sustained 11% margin with better collections can produce attractive returns without requiring a premium market multiple.
factor_audit.rationale: 4: price is not exuberant on unadjusted profit, but still requires better economics than the conservative base; no claim of a verified margin of safety.

factor_audit.name: Lot-discrete tradability
supporting_facts: Official master confirms 1,000-share lot, worth ₹114,300 at the reference price.
Secondary 20-session median 26,000 shares permits one lot/day at 5%; eight of 20 observations allow no whole lot at 5%.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Several secondary days show material volume, and the security is eligible in SM; this is not evidence of suspension.
factor_audit.rationale: NS: only 46 secondary observations and less than 60 sessions since listing, with no primary turnover or spread/circuit history. Do not fabricate zeros or fill a 60-day score from a 20-day proxy.
factor_audit.missing_evidence: Complete primary daily series, actual traded value, circuit/depth/spread and current trading restrictions.

BQS.rounding: Exact Decimal weights and contributions; displayed bounds use ROUND_HALF_UP to one decimal; exact numeric bounds retained.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Identity: G V Electricals Ltd, incorporated 28 February 1985 as G.V.Electricals Private Limited, converted to public company 4 November 2025; BSE SME 544859, trading symbol GVELECTRIC, ISIN INE1ZGR01024. Listing began 12 August 2026. The 19 October interoperable master confirms 11,279,190 issued shares and a 1,000-share eligible SM lot. Its GVELECTRI$ alias is not an NSE listing. The pre-listing ownership document explicitly says NSE not listed; the September upload is not a September-quarter shareholding report.

Research cutoff 20 October 2026, market reference 19 October 2026, five-year horizon to 19 October 2031, nominal INR pretax shareholder hurdle 15%. Financial history is standalone restated AS accounts, not Ind AS consolidated figures; there are no identified subsidiaries/NCI. Fiscal years end 31 March. All model money is ₹crore except per-share prices/lot calculations. Access occurred 21 October, but no later-dated events are incorporated. The ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is an analytical test, not a portfolio-size recommendation.

G1 Conditional: adverse controls evidence, no established severe integrity failure. G2 Hold: unexplained quantitative bank-return/books differences and inconsistent auditor-change disclosure. G3 Hold: real IPO receipt, unverified utilization and facility continuation. G4 Conditional: eligible security, incomplete primary liquidity evidence. No gate is silently converted from Hold to Fail. Confidence is High on exact identity, audited table transcription and statutory disclosures; Medium on operating durability and historical revenue attribution; Low on investable return, incremental-contract economics and executable liquidity. G3 Hold alone would not exclude quality comparisons; missing CAP and G2 reliability do so here.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The thirteen primitive factors are GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 6, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 2, BAL 4, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P 4 and L NS. Each has supporting and contrary evidence in the factor audit. CAP is not a neutral 5: its missing incremental-contract economics remain missing. R is not scored from a cash-positive model when its opening resources and banking assumptions are unverified. L is not scored from an incomplete secondary substitute.

BQS uses GOV 20%, MOAT 20%, REV 12%, DUR 10%, CAP 12%, CASH 10%, BAL 8%, EXEC 8%. Known contribution 3.84, coverage 88%, raw completion bounds 3.96–5.04, displayed 4.0–5.0; no point score. GQS means Growth Quality: REV 40%, DUR 20%, EARN 15%, CAP 15%, CASH 10%. Known contribution 4.55, coverage 85%, raw bounds 4.70–6.05. Persistent CASH 2 caps any completed GQS at 5, producing capped bounds 4.70–5.00, but does not justify assigning 5 or any other point.

IAS uses final BQS 25%, R 35%, D 20%, P 10%, L 10%. Known contribution 1.00, coverage 30%, broad raw bounds 1.70–8.00. Propagating BQS bounds narrows the mathematical interval to 2.44–6.76; neither interval is a confidence band or a return forecast. Exact Decimal arithmetic precedes half-up one-decimal display. There is no renormalization, midpoint imputation or ranking of missing points. All three ranking flags are false. No governance cap is applied because GOV 4/G1 Conditional do not meet the severe threshold; G3 Hold does not apply the failure-only IAS 3 cap.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company supplies field operations, maintenance, electrical infrastructure/network work and metering services to utilities and other customers. FY26 segment sales were O&M ₹120.2831 cr, infrastructure/network ₹22.9310 cr and metering ₹13.1988 cr. The economic engine is qualified labour deployment, site supervision, vehicles/equipment and customer certification, not a manufacturing plant with measurable utilization. Employee benefits ₹106.53 cr and transport ₹20.39 cr together dominate costs. Customer billing must fund wages, statutory remittances and deployment before cash is received.

Odisha contributes 69.05% of FY26 sales; Maharashtra 12.45%, Delhi 7.56%, Gujarat 6.63%, Rajasthan 3.61%, Uttar Pradesh 0.64% and Goa 0.07% show presence but not geographical balance. Utilities account for 79.10% and integrated utilities 9.04%. Top-ten customers contribute 94.76% of sales, top three 64.79% and the largest 33.33%. Ranked names are not disclosed in the concentration table, so logos are not used to guess who owes which receivable.

Under AS policies, manpower/service revenue follows work/attendance and customer acknowledgment, while EPC revenue uses percentage completion and contractual certification. Unbilled work ₹0.9336 cr is separate from trade receivables; retention/EMD/security deposits ₹4.2089 cr are separately committed operating capital. Neither is freely available cash. Most offices are short-term rentals; rent is retained in operating costs and no artificial Ind AS lease liability is added. The cash cycle, contract renewal, staff productivity and customer concentration are more useful operating metrics than an unsupported factory-capacity narrative.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The defensible part of the business is local operating knowledge, tender credentials, a deployed workforce and the inconvenience of replacing a functioning utility service team. FY26 repeat revenue 88.29% and decades of operating history provide evidence of relationships. But tender price competition, labour mobility and a concentrated customer base limit pricing power. There is no evidence of protected intellectual property, a network effect, exclusive distribution rights or independently measured switching-cost economics. Repeat share fell from 97.14% in FY25, which weakens an automatic annuity interpretation.

Three peer lenses are used without pretending comparability. The prospectus reports Rajesh Power FY26 revenue ₹1,627.94 cr, EBITDA margin 12.46% and PAT ₹143.20 cr, far greater scale and a different EPC mix. Parth Electricals has revenue ₹198.00 cr, EBITDA margin 10.53% and PAT ₹14.24 cr, closer revenue scale but material product/manufacturing differences. Their prospectus P/E snapshots are dated 20 July 2026 and are not used as current trading multiples. KEC International's own FY26 consolidated release reports revenue ₹23,506 cr, EBITDA margin 7.1% and working capital 137 days. It is a large diversified EPC counterbenchmark showing that execution scale does not abolish cash-cycle risk, not a direct small-company valuation anchor.

MOAT 4 therefore recognizes relationships without assuming a franchise. Failure modes include losing a major tender, wage escalation without repricing, delayed certification and customer concentration turning a seemingly recurring contract into a funding drain. The company's FY26 margin is not automatically superior economics until collection and contract-level return evidence support it.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Use the consistent restated series: FY23 ₹104.2224 cr, FY24 ₹111.7956 cr, FY25 ₹131.2356 cr and FY26 ₹156.4129 cr. Annual additions are ₹7.5732 cr, ₹19.4400 cr and ₹25.1773 cr; respective growth rates are 7.27%, 17.39% and 19.18%. Three-year CAGR is 14.49%; two-year CAGR 18.28%. Original audited FY22 revenue ₹79.4871 cr implies a four-year scale CAGR 18.44%, but that older statement is not mixed into a supposedly uniform profit/return history. A comparable five-year series is unavailable.

The FY26 ₹25.1773 cr addition comprises O&M+₹16.2723 cr, infrastructure/network+₹12.8664 cr and metering −₹3.9614 cr. Growth is therefore not uniformly accelerating across activities. No acquisition-led consolidation change is identified; it appears organic in the accounting perimeter, but the disclosure does not separately quantify labour-volume growth, price increases, project mix and contract additions. The ₹553.70 cr headline book is 3.54× FY26 sales, but variable service frameworks cannot be divided mechanically by years to predict revenue.

REV 6 follows the 10–15% consistent three-year anchor. FY26 strength is meaningful, but one annual step and a presentation repeating March accounts do not satisfy the two-half/four-quarter test for a trajectory bonus. September's data-centre strategy is a proposed growth vector, not confirmed incremental sales. This avoids confusing a large addressable market or an order headline with verified revenue conversion.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Growth requires much more working capital than fixed assets. From FY23 to FY26 the operating IC bridge rises ₹15.0487 cr to ₹54.0880 cr, a ₹39.0393 cr commitment increase. Of this, ₹33.5134 cr is ONWC, ₹1.2393 cr fixed-deposit backing, ₹0.0830 cr retention/deposit movement and ₹4.2036 cr net PPE. Three-year cash capex less D&A ₹4.2637 cr reconciles to net PPE after ₹0.0601 cr disposal/book-value rounding. The financing-side IC bridge matches all four year ends, so the denominator is not casually equated with annual capex.

At 33% normalized operating tax, NOPAT rises ₹2.491261 cr to ₹10.292540 cr and ΔNOPAT/ΔIC is 19.98%. Tax sensitivities yield 18.49–22.32%, compared with a judgmental 14–18% nominal INR post-tax cost-of-capital range. This is a meaningful accounting proxy, but not enough for CAP: ₹9.7817 cr of the ₹11.6437 cr EBIT increase is mechanically attributable to changed margin on the FY26 revenue base, versus ₹1.8620 cr from sales growth at the FY23 margin. It does not identify which new contracts earned the returns or whether they collected. No mature-cohort cash margins or contract-level capital bridge are supplied. Five-year and lagged commissioned-return tests remain unavailable, not zero.

The bottom-up base model grows O&M 12/12/10/10/8%, infrastructure 18/16/14/12/10%, and metering 8/8/8/7/6% over five annual periods. It requires additional receivables, retention, FD backing, inventory and capex and does not turn frameworks into guaranteed backlog. Base margin 9% is below FY26's 10.90%; lower creditor funding is assumed so growth is not financed indefinitely by delayed taxes/wages. The IPO could fund this path, but the actual October resource bridge is missing. GQS remains NS at 85% coverage, with capped completion bounds 4.70–5.00 because persistent weak cash realization overrides attractive headline earnings growth.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Capital allocation is mixed. Connected advances ₹4.9273 cr in FY24, almost 29% of equity, were reduced to nil by FY26. That recovery is positive; it does not retroactively establish the original terms were minority-friendly. FY25 connected service purchases from Nucleus ₹2.7574 cr fell to nil in FY26. Director/KMP disclosures should be evaluated in aggregate, not by selecting one ₹36 lakh remuneration line. The IPO's ₹33.4904 cr net fresh funds are intended for debt repayment ₹6 cr, working capital ₹22 cr and general purposes ₹5.4904 cr. Secondary promoter sales and the ₹3.25 cr OFS are not company funding.

Compliance is the sharper concern. FY26 delayed GST ₹22.6023 cr, PF ₹9.1139 cr and ESIC ₹1.2340 cr involve numerous instances; maximum disclosed delays 84,214 and 148 days respectively. These are delayed payment flows, not all still-outstanding liabilities. Management says amounts were remitted with charges, yet recurring statutory interest/penalties ₹0.7346 cr are retained in normalized costs. Bank-return/books discrepancies repeat, while the FY26 CARO statement of no auditor resignation conflicts with the prospectus's 16 July 2025 predecessor resignation. The stated reason was preoccupation, not a disclosed scope dispute. The audit opinion is unmodified and no lender default/fraud was reported.

Dated delivery checks: the 30 June order schedule expected Odisha metering work to finish in August 2026 and Ajmer in September 2026; completion/renewal proof was not found, so status is unresolved, not failed. A Mumbai fault-repair contract runs to May 2027, not yet due at cutoff. The 31 July corrigendum corrected collateral ownership, promoter proprietorships and ROC inaccuracies. On 4 August an independent director vacated office following disqualification arising from another company's filings; replacement and a three-day IPO extension/withdrawal window were disclosed. The August fresh allotment was delivered, but debt-repayment/working-capital use remains unverified. This is a control-and-delivery watchlist with GOV 4/EXEC 5, not an unsupported assertion of company misconduct.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Comparable FY23/FY24/FY25/FY26 figures in ₹crore: revenue 104.2224/111.7956/131.2356/156.4129; calculated operating EBITDA 4.0403/6.1389/8.0436/17.0495; PAT 1.9089/2.8032/4.6608/10.4657; CFO 0.8724/0.3867/1.0818/−3.3099; cash capex 0.1945/1.1186/2.9276/3.0604; gross debt 4.5011/4.9474/7.8419/16.4713; equity 14.2475/17.0507/23.1999/33.6656. Embedded annual rows retain operating capital, claims, cash, margins and exact definitions. FY24/FY25 original profit is restated down, so an aggregator's mixed-history CAGR is not used.

The FY26 cash bridge starts PBT ₹14.3001 cr, removes FD interest ₹0.2035 cr and adds D&A ₹1.6875 cr, finance ₹1.3100 cr, disposal loss ₹0.0101 cr and gratuity provision ₹2.8626 cr to reach ₹19.9668 cr before working capital. Receivables absorb ₹20.2731 cr, inventory ₹2.2087 cr, short advances ₹1.0685 cr and other current assets ₹0.5032 cr; retention/other non-current release ₹0.4497 cr, suppliers ₹0.4480 cr and other current liabilities ₹3.8017 cr partly offset. Cash before tax is ₹0.6126 cr; paid tax ₹3.9226 cr produces CFO −₹3.3099 cr, subject to source rounding. Capex reduces investing cash flow, not CFO. Reported three-year CFO/PAT is −10.27%, or −24.09% after finance costs classified in financing; three-year reported FCF is −₹8.948 cr.

Average-receivable-days proxy rises from 79.39 in FY25 to 95.72 in FY26; closing days rise 85.89 to 119.38. Total revenue substitutes for undisclosed credit sales. Inventory/payable days and CCC are not invented using incompatible service/payroll costs. Disclosed overdue receivables beyond six months improve from ₹4.0563 cr to ₹1.1290 cr, contrary evidence worth preserving, while management records no allowance. An unmodified audit is not a collection guarantee.

FY26 average-capital ROIC at 33% tax is 24.03%, not the company's 31.13% pre-tax ROCE. The three-year incremental 19.98% proxy is separately qualified. March current maturities ₹1.0682 cr already sit inside short debt, and gratuity ₹6.7612 cr is a separate claim. Only ₹1.4606 cr cash is clearly cash-equivalent;₹4.5527 cr FD is not automatically free. Payroll/statutory balances remain in ONWC, not duplicated as debt. Equity value must use 11,279,190 post-issue shares: FY26 current-share EPS ₹9.28 versus weighted pre-IPO ₹12.64. Fresh-share count dilution 36.24% is real; the split/bonus alone is not. The financial model records source rounding, reclassifications and the exact operating-to-financing IC reconciliation rather than forcing spurious precision.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹114.30 the market capitalization is ₹128.9211 cr. Dividing FY26 PAT by current shares gives ₹9.2788 EPS and 12.32× P/E, not the prospectus's pre-IPO EPS. An old-balance EV illustration adds March debt ₹16.4713 cr, deducts March free cash ₹1.4606 cr and mutual-fund market value ₹0.9036 cr, and shows gratuity ₹6.7612 cr separately. It is not live EV because the August IPO intervened. Operating EBITDA removes other income and retains recurring penalties; normalized tax 33% is higher than the statutory 25.17% because actual disallowances and cash-tax timing matter.

All five annual model rows are embedded in canonical JSON. The analytical opening cash ₹29.2426 cr is March cash plus ₹39 cr gross fresh proceeds less ₹5.2180 cr remaining issue expenses and planned ₹6 cr debt repayment; the ₹0.2916 cr March IPO prepaid is conditionally treated as already paid within the total expense budget, not charged twice, with no claim that the entire balance remained in October. Bear/base/bull use explicit segment growth, EBITDA margins 5.5–7%/9%/10.5–11%, receivable days 155→135/115→100/105→90 and terminal EBITDA multiples 6/8/10. Total capex 2% and D&A 1.1% of sales are separate estimates; maintenance capex is not pretended equal to depreciation. Payroll, statutory creditor normalization, retention, FD backing, debt amortization, interest, cash tax and gratuity roll forward. No new debt plug funds a deficit. Only terminal cash above the operating floor is added; debt/gratuity are deducted once.

Conditional five-year bear/base/bull shareholder CAGRs are −11.43%/10.40%/25.38%. Their 15%-hurdle entry prices are ₹30.97/₹93.19/₹176.04, scenario diagnostics rather than a recommended range. Base-margin minus/plus 2 points moves return to 3.78%/15.73%; exit multiples 6/10 move it to 5.01%/14.91%. A 30-day collection delay reduces base return to 8.07%; combining this delay with ₹20 cr less opening cash creates a year 1 shortfall and null ordinary return. R remains NS despite cash-positive hypothetical upper-resource paths because usable resources and continuing facilities are not independently verified. Every ordinary return and ordinary hurdle-entry field is null; numbers are stored only in explicitly named conditional_hypothetical fields. A hypothetical path that fails its cash floor also has null conditional return, unless separately labeled as rescue.

Reverse solving the full base cash path for 15% at today's price requires about 17.57% aggregate revenue CAGR, terminal revenue ₹351.33 cr and 9% EBITDA margin, not simply multiple expansion. This is a testable expectation, not company guidance. Sensitivities preserve all annual rows and explicit limits; no probability-weighted expected return is claimed.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not a sudden end to Indian power spending. It is loss/repricing of a concentrated service contract while wages, statutory remittances and bank collateral obligations still have to be met. The modeled bear lowers first-year O&M 15%, infrastructure 30% and metering 20%, compresses EBITDA to 5.5%, delays receivables to 155 days and reduces the benefit from operating creditors to 4% of sales. It pays 20% of ₹8.2836 cr outstanding guarantees plus the ₹0.4399 cr GST contingency once, rather than misclassifying every guarantee as debt.

With the optimistic pro-forma opening cash intact, this bear is hypothetically fundable but ends near ₹62.30/share, a 45.50% capital decline and −11.43% five-year CAGR. That illustrates how permanent value impairment can occur without bankruptcy. Actual available cash is unknown. A separate bear-plus-₹20 cr-consumed-opening-cash path needs rescue from year 1. Its explicitly hypothetical equity raise at 70% of the entry quote totals ₹7.4438 cr, dilutes old holders 7.62% and yields −16.19% to existing shares before investor taxes. The main rescue explicitly assumes zero issue costs, an optimistic simplification. At 5% issue costs the gross raise rises to ₹7.8356 cr, fees ₹0.3918 cr, dilution 7.99% and conditional rescue return −16.26%. At 10% costs gross funding is ₹8.2709 cr, fees ₹0.8271 cr, dilution 8.40% and return −16.33%. Fees are paid once from proceeds. No rescue funding availability is claimed. All ordinary returns and hurdle-entry prices remain null until actual financing is verified, including cash-positive hypothetical cases; these numeric results are conditional hypothetical diagnostics only.

Receivables can also be overstated or collect late; a bank drawing-power reduction can compound rather than diversify that risk. The current model does not prove those events will occur. It identifies the thesis-break variables: persistent failure to collect certified receivables, a material unreconciled bank-asset gap, unavailable cash-credit renewal, or diversion of fresh funds from disclosed needs. Conversely, clean bank confirmations, actual IPO utilization and post-March cash realization would weaken the bear case. No precise probability of default is assigned on missing evidence.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold price appreciation over five years requires 37.97% annual shareholder compounding; tenfold requires 58.49%. A mechanical solve using the base 9% margin, 8× terminal EBITDA, unchanged original shares and the full working-capital/claim bridge requires terminal revenues about ₹955.61 cr for 5× and ₹1,884.05 cr for 10×. These correspond to 43.62% and 64.50% revenue CAGRs from ₹156.41 cr. They are not simple rerating targets.

Crucially, the same annual paths fail the funding floor: the 5× solve first fails in year 2 and reaches a diagnostic gap about ₹77.57 cr; the 10× solve fails in year 1 with a gap about ₹261.22 cr. Therefore the ordinary shareholder-return fields are null for both. Raising equity would change the share denominator and make the target harder; raising debt would require actual sanctioned capacity and interest support. The scenario's mathematical price target does not establish a feasible investment outcome.

The current ₹553.70 cr headline contract frameworks, concentrated customers, labour deployment needs and slow collections do not evidence the required scaling. A successful larger-contractor outcome is possible in principle, but no 5×/10× designation is justified. Demonstrated incremental margins, retention/renewals, staffing productivity, collection cash and a non-destructive financing plan must precede such a claim.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Collections: baseline March receivables ₹51.1556 cr and closing 119.38 days. Seek audited/reviewed post-March receipts and customer confirmations. Warning: days stay above 120 as revenue grows; severe stress above 150 or fresh material disputed balances.
2. Cash realization: three-year CFO/PAT −10.27%. Require positive operating cash after finance and repeated improvement, not one-period creditor stretching. Negative CFO with rising PAT keeps the cash-quality cap.
3. Bank reconciliation: March 2026 gap ₹5.3195 cr and September 2025 gap ₹11.2271 cr. Obtain an itemized bank-accepted reconciliation; unresolved or enlarging discrepancies keep G2 on Hold.
4. IPO utilization: reconcile ₹33.4904 cr net funds, ₹6 cr planned debt repayment and ₹22 cr working-capital use to bank statements/reviewed accounts. A headline “utilized” certificate without remaining cash and claims is insufficient.
5. Borrowing access: May CC ₹13.9447 cr/₹14 cr. Verify renewed sanction, eligible drawing power, actual draw, security and any covenant/renewal conditions. The model assumes no incremental sanctioned facility.
6. Compliance: require evidence of timely PF/ESIC/GST payments after listing and closure of disclosed tax/labour matters. New repeated delays or material fines weaken governance and operating funding confidence.
7. Contract execution: reconcile opening frameworks, fresh awards, cancellations, execution and receipts; verify August/September 2026 metering completion or renewals. Track largest customer share against 33.33% and Odisha against 69.05%.
8. Margin and incremental returns: FY26 EBITDA 10.90% versus FY25 6.13%. Demand contract/cohort contribution, labour utilization, collection and capital commitment, rather than using current ROCE as proof of new-investment returns.
9. Disclosure controls: reconcile auditor-resignation contradiction, presentation EBITDA headline and CSR narrative inconsistencies; compare subsequent signed filings rather than stale website templates.
10. Tradability and claims: obtain 60 listed sessions of primary actual turnover, zero-trade/circuit/depth evidence and updated share/pledge/encumbrance disclosures. Recompute the 1,000-share lot test before any purchase; a lot change or dilution requires refreshing every per-share/exit calculation.

These are research checkpoints, not an automatically authorized monitoring service or promise of future action.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: research watchlist, unproven contract-services growth; not an established compounder and not a scored investment candidate. There is evidence of revenue growth, recurring operating relationships and completed equity funding. There is also persistent weak cash realization, high customer/geographical concentration, incomplete incremental economics and material reliability/funding gaps. A low trailing P/E on a high-margin year does not resolve them.

BQS and GQS remain NS because CAP is missing; G2 independently restricts a numerical quality ranking. IAS is NS because Q, R and L are missing and G2/G3 are unresolved. G3 Hold by itself is not a reason to exclude a quality comparison, and it is not treated as a demonstrated funding failure. GOV 4 does not trigger an unsupported “Avoid: governance” label. This separation matters: an ordinary operating business can deserve further research while the current shares remain unsuitable for a favorable new-purchase conclusion.

Conditional action is to obtain the bank/book and post-IPO funding evidence first, then recompute sustainable margins, cash conversion, incremental returns and primary lot-discrete exit capacity. The base model's ₹93.19 hurdle price is an arithmetic conditional threshold, not an entry recommendation or a substitute for passing gates. At ₹114.30 the conditional base return is below 15%; a lower price would not repair unreliable accounting or unavailable finance. No portfolio sizing, order, target-price promise or publication action is implied.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary hierarchy: the 10 August final prospectus supersedes overlapping DRHP periods and provides detailed restated FY24–FY26 accounts; the 30 March DRHP supplies the comparable FY23 opening period. The FY26 annual report's scanned auditor/CARO pages were inspected visually, with unmodified opinion and adverse details both retained. July/August corrigenda and allotment establish governance events and completed fundraising. The 19 October official interoperable master plus its field specification establish exact security identity, shares and lot. The issuer's pre-listing shareholding page is not misdated as September-quarter data. Secondary price/OHLCV is used only with its lower confidence and missing-primary-history caveat.

Source ledger entries include working URLs, dated locators, read scope and SHA 256 hashes for downloaded originals. Canonical JSON embeds historical inputs, operating/financing capital bridges, annual scenario paths, financing tests, claim treatment, sensitivities, reverse expectations, discrete liquidity and limitations. Reproduction uses build_model.py then build_dossier.py; source/model tests and the common validator are separate from investment judgment. Raw PDFs, extracted full source text and individual shareholding records are excluded from Library packages because unnecessary personal identifiers may appear in public filings. Original source URLs/hashes and identifier-free evidence preserve provenance.

Open questions are explicit: actual October cash/debt and IPO utilization; bank-accepted collateral reconciliation; current facility availability; attributable mature-contract returns; primary actual traded-value/spread/circuit history; recent contract renewals/completions; promoter encumbrances; and current legal/CSR closure evidence. The September deck repeats March financials, not fresh results. Its page 4 EBITDA ₹17.49 cr differs from detailed ₹17.0494 cr; the latter is consistent with the prospectus apart from ₹0.0001 cr rounding. The annual report says no auditor resignation despite the prospectus's dated resignation. Its CSR narrative also needs reconciliation; no unverified extra liability is booked as fact.

Major assumptions are five analytical annual periods from the quote date, 33% normalized tax, explicit segment growth and margin cases, 2% total capex, continued existing facilities, no new debt plug, an operating cash floor and 6/8/10× terminal EBITDA. They are analyst scenarios, not management guidance. All ordinary shareholder-return and entry-price fields stay null while financing is unverified; cash-positive scenario figures use explicitly conditional hypothetical fields. Missing data stays NS; absence of a retrieved filing is not proof of a zero balance, no trade or a missed commitment.

capital_analysis.limitation: Three-year proxy is arithmetically meaningful but not attributable to mature incremental contracts: FY26 margin expansion on the installed business dominates, restated bank collateral values remain unreconciled, and no project/cohort margin or collection economics are reported. No CAP score is inferred from current ROCE.

claim_register.treatment: Included in ONWC; conservative normalization releases their funding benefit. No duplicate enterprise-value deduction.

claim_register.claim: Fixed deposits, retention and operating cash
claim_register.treatment: All FD prudentially excluded from freely available cash; lien is only partly quantified. Retention remains operating capital. Only excess terminal cash above explicit floor is added to equity.
AS accounts, short office rentals expensed; no identified capitalized lease liability, no subsidiary/NCI. Do not add an Ind AS lease claim without also rebasing earnings.

limitations: Post-IPO actual use of cash and actual debt balances are not verified by cutoff. The cash bridge is an upper-resource thought experiment, not financing evidence.
Existing cash-credit continuation, bank-accepted drawing power and renewal terms are not verified. R is NS even if a hypothetical case is cash-positive.

No automatic plug debt. All ordinary return and hurdle-entry fields are null until actual financing is verified. Numeric returns exist only in explicitly conditional hypothetical fields when that hypothetical path funds its cash floor. A separately labeled rescue uses equity at70% of entry price, zero issue costs in the main illustration, and5%/10% gross-proceeds cost sensitivities; availability is not assumed.
Tax and gratuity timing use normalized assumptions; maintenance capex is not disclosed separately. Total capex remains the reinvestment deduction.
Terminal EBITDA multiples 6/8/10 are scenario judgments for a small concentrated contractor, not contemporaneous peer averages. No reinvestment-free terminal growth is assumed.
FD pledges are incompletely classified. Releasing FD would increase cash but may impair guarantees/drawing power; no free-cash benefit assumed.
No dividend stream modeled. Any future distribution must be funded and cannot be added without reducing cash.
